terms.comment: The everyday word for a branch, an osier, a whip that bends. It has other common senses: sticky or tough, and above all slow, sluggish, at ease (lentus in umbrā, Verg. E. 1.4), so let the thing that bends make the sense clear (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: that can be bent; of a voice or a mind, pliant, adaptable
evidence: Cic. Att. 10.11.1: nihil nōn flexibile ad bonitātem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The word for flexibility of mind or manner: a voice (Cic. N.D. 2.146), a person open to persuasion; in a bad sense, fickle (quid potest esse tam flexibile, Cic. Lael. 92).

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Ov.; in prose Plin.
evidence: Plin. NH 16.219: ulmus et fraxinus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: flectitur obsequiō curvātus ab arbore rāmus: frangis, sī vīrēs experiēre tuās
phrases.english: a branch bends from the tree if you go along with it; try your strength on it and you’ll break it

phrases.latin: jamque arbore summā cōnfluere et lentīs ūvam dēmittere rāmīs
phrases.english: and now they gather at the treetop and hang like a bunch of grapes from the bending branches

phrases.latin: haec implet lentō calathōs ē vīmine nexōs
phrases.english: one fills baskets woven of pliant osier
